chapter: Glaser, the Arcadia and bands of 1939-41
title: Return to the Savoy and meeting Joe Glaser
summary: At the Savoy Roy hosted young trumpeters, and Glaser demanded he come to his office or not work.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And I came to the Savoy, and all the cats used to come up there and sit in -- Dizzy, Joe Guy, Charlie, Bobby Moore, all the little trumpet players that was around in those days. And they know my records better than I did. They all knew the solos, I mean. So they would sit in.

And that's when I had my meeting with Joe Glaser. I had seen Joe Glaser once in Chicago, because that's when everybody...by me being on the air, everybody was taking notice of me then, you know. I had won those polls and things, and I was winning Second Place, and somebody said, "Well, why let a dead man beat him out all the time?" -- Bix was beating me out all the time, you know. They said, "How about people that's living?" So they turned around and they let me win First!

Then Joe Glaser came up... No, he came in one night to listen to me, you know. And he walked in, and he just more or less "Oh shit," you know, and walked out. So I said, "Okay," you know, because I knew the story about him and I didn't want to be with him anyhow. In fact, I didn't want to be with no one after this cat in Chicago who kept me from going to California. It might have been a whole different future for me had I went to Hollywood at that time, you know.
So when I come off the stand at the Savoy, he was

there, and he said, "Listen, be at my office tomorrow at ten o'clock. I've got a job for you." I said, "I won't be there." "Why?" "Because I've got something I'm doing... I don't want nobody to book me." He said, "You be there or you won't work around New York."
